MEASURED RESULT: THE GATE HAS EXCEEDED ITS OWN RUNTIME LIMIT. This is no longer a projection.

  fixture ready signal   11:36:52
  observed               12:10:32
  measured elapsed       33 min 40 s        against the 30-minute gate  -> EXCEEDED
  worker CPU             27 min 16 s
  worker RSS             2.04 GiB, still falling   against the 4 GiB gate -> never approached

The runner starts measuring when the fixture-ready signal appears (run-crossnobis-scale-gate.R:53), so analysis_seconds is already past 1800 and runtime_pass will be FALSE when the run completes. The process is still going.

TWO THINGS THIS SETTLES

1. Dense local shrinkage at whole-brain scale is RUNTIME-bound, not memory-bound. Peak RSS was about 2.4 GiB against a 4 GiB budget and has been falling steadily under gc. Every memory-side concern on this epic, including my own earlier projections, was aimed at the wrong constraint. The binding cost is the per-support k-by-k solve work across 52416 nodes and six edges.

2. It fails in the MOST FAVOURABLE configuration available: q = 2, three partitions, six ordered edges, and a local covariance singular for 84% of supports. There is no cheaper statistically-shaped workload for this path. Both remedies for the degeneracy - observations 32 to 200, or partitions 3 to 6 - multiply the dominant cost 5-6x, so a non-degenerate fixture is further outside the gate, not closer to it.

CONCLUSION FOR EPIC 8, which its own acceptance already names

"If dense local shrinkage misses the gate, version 0.1 supports brain-scale diagonal metrics and explicitly scopes dense metrics to smaller supports/node sets."

That clause is now the measured outcome. Recommend Epic 8 close by recording:
  - brain-scale diagonal / identity metrics: SUPPORTED. Same 52k-voxel volume, 166 s end to end.
  - dense local metrics at whole-brain node counts: NOT SUPPORTED in 0.1, exceeds 30 minutes.
  - a declared supported ceiling for dense metrics, found by re-running the gate at reduced node
    counts until it fits, and stated in node count and support size rather than left implicit.

That is a genuine and useful 0.1 scope statement. Reporting it is a stronger result than a pass would have been, and it is exactly what the epic set out to establish.
